summary: Sixth cold read of the spec, run at the requirements gate. Nine gaps: eight resolved in the amended spec, the ninth an owner choice on catalog overflow, settled as names always with details degrading past a ceiling.
gaps: The promised complete invocation descriptor cannot be derived for every binding kind: MCP-pattern bindings carry only server and tool patterns and adapters only an opaque reference, neither with an argument schema.
'Every grant always renders' has no feasible bound against a fixed 1,500-character guidance section and a deterministic truncating renderer.
The criterion removing the per-capability runtime block while preserving the dispatcher unchanged is self-contradictory, because the dispatcher description points at that block.

The document-tool authority model is incomplete and internally conflicting: the scheduled read surface of decision 0106 is an explicit list that does not include the view tool, while the write-authority criterion would make a read-only scheduled viewer unusable.
Interactive write approval is unspecified: joining the scheduler mutation set only removes tools from autonomous surfaces and does not make attended writes ask, which decision 0107 requires.

Canonical ownership does not resolve the shared-group case, and no document reference grammar or discovery path is defined, so a group editor has no way to address the prompt without the forbidden authority source.
The revision fence does not specify the existing whole-document update protocol, its returned revision, or its conflict result, so no retry contract exists for an attended updater.
The document command contract is incomplete: omitted, invalid and empty-document semantics for ranges, insertion points on an empty document, and returned revisions on mutation are all unstated.
'Rate-limited' and 'deterministic replay' are not falsifiable: no limit, window, key, durability choice or response, and no harness or fixture that proves the descriptor caused the call.
contradictions: The spec both removed the per-capability runtime block and preserved the dispatcher contract unchanged, while that dispatcher's description directs the model to the removed block.
resolutions: Spec now defines a closed descriptor union per binding kind and states that kinds without an argument schema carry the reachable tool identity and say so, rather than an invented shape.

Owner ruled the ceiling behaviour: the section grows from the granted set up to a stated ceiling, non-granted material is dropped first, then descriptions, then entries compact; past the ceiling every granted id still renders without its descriptor and an overflow diagnostic is recorded. No grant is reduced to a count or omitted.
Spec now updates the dispatcher description text to point at the catalog, while pinning its input schema, risk classification and host enforcement unchanged by test.

Spec now separates read and write authority: reading needs the job read authority a caller already has and the view tool joins decision 0106's explicit scheduled read surface, which this story extends by naming it there; only writes require write authority.
Spec now classifies the write tools high-risk so they ask in normal auto mode per decision 0107, rather than inheriting a default classification.

Spec now defines the reference grammar as an opaque job-scoped key discovered from the job read, never itself a source of authority, and authorizes a shared-group job for an acting person the host records as a member of that group.

Spec now gives the whole-document update the same optional expected revision: stale is refused with the actual revision so the caller re-reads and retries, omitted behaves as today, and every successful write returns its revision.

Spec now states omitted, out-of-bounds and inverted range behaviour, empty-document reads, line-zero prepend as the only valid insertion into an empty document, an error past the last line, and a returned revision on every mutation; criteria 7 and 7b prove them.

Spec now sets the limiter at ten failures per document and caller per minute, process-local and bounding probing within a run, with a distinct error and criterion 12c; and the replay criterion now names the harness and fixture and adds a negative control proving the descriptor causes the call.
open_items: Non-blocking: a capability lookup tool would remove the ceiling entirely and is deferred as out of scope for this story.

rounds.question: If an agent's granted capabilities will not fit the prompt section, what should it see?
